subject: Tenant network acceptance & activation checklist
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@medtech.io>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: netops@medtech.io
Date: 2028-06-13T09:17:00Z
Subject: Tenant network acceptance & activation checklist

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the onboarding kickoff yesterday. We're ready to move from intake to activation and need to lock down the network acceptance items so our infra team can schedule the cutover. A few asks we want to confirm up front: 

- Can you confirm the egress IPs we should allow and the expected outbound ports (we typically whitelist 443 and 5222 for telemetry).
- Do you require any inbound firewall rules to reach a bastion/jumpbox? If so, please provide IP ranges and port list.
- For KMS/HSM integration: we use AWS KMS. Do you have a preferred pattern (cross-account role vs. customer-managed key)?
- Any cert fingerprints we should expect from the control plane endpoints?

Attached: our current tenant-egress-ip-list.csv (placeholder) and internal network diagram. If you can send a concise acceptance checklist we can slot into our change window next week (Wed/Thu preferred).

Samantha
Netops Lead | MedTech Systems
Samantha.cho@medtech.io

Attachments: tenant-egress-ip-list.csv (text/csv), medtech-internal-network-diagram.png (image)

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@medtech.io>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-06-13T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Tenant network acceptance & activation checklist

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Attaching our onboarding checklist (PDF) and a short runbook excerpt below to make scheduling easier. Short answers up front:

- Egress IPs: 34.203.12.45, 34.203.12.46 (TCP 443, 80 for health checks; telemetry uses outbound 443).
- Inbound: We do not require inbound from the internet to customer VPCs for normal operation. If you want a managed bastion for debug, we recommend a customer-provisioned jumpbox in a private subnet that initiates an outbound connection to our ops relay (no inbound firewall changes needed).
- KMS: cross-account IAM role is our recommended pattern (we'll provide the role ARN). Customer-managed CMKs are supported if you prefer; we will need the key ARN and grant.
- Cert fingerprints: the control plane provides rotating certs; we publish current SHA256 fingerprints in the onboarding doc link below.

Quick acceptance checklist (please confirm each):
1) Tenant egress IPs added to your outbound allowlist.
2) NAT/egress path verified for outbound 443 to our IPs from the app subnets.
3) Route tables in private subnets include NAT/IGW for outbound egress (if using NAT) and no public IPs on workload interfaces.
4) KMS access pattern confirmed (cross-account role or CMK ARN).
5) Audit logging: ensure flow logs (VPC) are enabled aimed at the monitoring bucket we agreed on.
6) Maintenance window: please pick Wed/Thu 02:00–05:00 UTC for final cutover if possible.

I'll follow up with the role ARN and a short test plan.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai

Attachments: redwood_onboarding_checklist_v1.pdf (pdf)

Samantha / Kimberly — quick preflight update from infra:

- I validated reachability from MedTech's listed NAT IPs to 34.203.12.45/46 over 443 from our preflight probes — good.
- KMS: we will send the role ARN today (redwood-kms-crossacct-prod) and a minimal permission set (Encrypt/Decrypt, GenerateDataKey) — please apply the least-privilege IAM policy and grant to the ARN.
- Flow logs: please confirm the account/bucket name you want the logs delivered to; we recommend a 30-day retention for onboarding evidence.

Next steps: Kim will open a short test plan (smoke traffic + telemetry verification). Once CHG-45981 is scheduled for Thu 02:00–05:00 UTC, we'll standby for the change window and do a coordinated cutover.
